newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Caracas shares end at record on electric rate hike.
newsitem.headline: Caracas shares end at record on electric rate hike.

text.p: The Caracas Stock Exchange general index surged to a sixth consecutive record high in heavy trade as a rate increase for market leader Electricidad de Caracas counteracted profit-taking, brokers said.
According to preliminary figures from the exchange, the market's 19-share index rose 2.03 percent to 8,566.13.
Electricidad jumped 43.00 bolivars to 692.00 bolivars on news that it had been awarded an increase in tariffs.
No official percentage increase in rates was announced, but brokers and analysts calculated it at more than 50 percent over the next six months -- above market expectations.
"It's great for Electricidad. It's much more than I would have expected," one local analyst said.
The apparent size of the rate increase made the stock jumped on the news despite the fact that the announcement had been widely expected for several weeks.

Despite Electricidad's rise, the market in general was hit by profit-taking a after a strong five-day rally. A total of 16 stocks rose, 27 fell and six closed flat in busy trade of 20.953 billion bolivars ($43.2 million).
The size of trade reflected strong foreign interest in the market.

Among other leading stocks, telephone company CANTV rose 55 bolivars to 2980.00 bolivars, while cement company Vencemos class 1 stock fell 15.00 to 620.00 bolivars and its class 2 stock fell 20.00 to 490.00 bolivars.
The composite .MRCP Merinvest index, which includes CANTV, rose 2.02 percent to 135.27.
Barring any new developments or announcements, brokers said stocks would likely fall Friday on profit-taking. But the underlying trend of the market remains bullish, they stressed.
